t: This is the site of the Foundling Hospital in Bloomsbury, a children's home founded in 1739 by the sea captain Thomas Coram. It was set up for the education and maintenance of exposed and deserted young children, and is said to be the world's first incorporated charity. Here, the word hospital meant hospitality, though the committee did put children's health first, fighting smallpox, fevers and dysentery. Two people are buried here: Charles Abbott, Baron Tenterden, who rose from a Canterbury barber's family to become Lord Chief Justice, and the antiquarian Daniel Rowland.
